content:
claire: FYI — product is planning an April rollout for the new routing policy changes. Need a short changelog blurb + a tiny migration note and one SDK snippet update. Who can own the docs PR?

jason: I can pick up the PR. what's the cutoff date for copy?

claire: target ship is 2026-04-07, cutoff for docs content is 2026-04-02 EOD. keep it short: feature intro + 1 known issue and link to migration guide.

emily: ok I'll draft. can you share the final wording for the behavioral change in routing (engineers gave 2 variants)? also need an example showing how to opt into the new fallback behavior in the JS SDK.

marc: short summary from eng: we now route by policy that prefers low-latency variants first, then cost-fallbacks. default behavior unchanged for existing customers. new opt-in: "prefer_latency": true in routing config. edge case: when using streaming + fallback, clients may see a short partial stream before the fallback completes — we'll include that as a known issue.

marc: suggested changelog copy: "Routing policy update: introduce an opt-in low-latency routing mode that prioritizes latency-optimized model variants. Existing integrations keep current behavior unless you enable the new setting. See migration guide for compatibility notes and SDK examples."

emily: thanks — that reads well. for the known issue I propose: "Known issue: streaming responses can emit a short partial batch when the system triggers a model fallback. If your app expects strictly atomic streams, use the retry-on-failure policy or disable streaming while you migrate."

jason: here are two minimal SDK snippets we should surface. short JS example to enable the new routing opt-in:

```js
// JS SDK (v2.x) opt into low-latency routing
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'rwk-1',
  prompt: 'Summarize the meeting',
  routing: { prefer_latency: true }
});
console.log(res.text);
```

```py
# Python SDK opt-in
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='rwk-1', prompt='Summarize the meeting', routing={'prefer_latency': True})
print(resp.text)
```

emily: perfect. I'll include both and a short note on the streaming fallback quirk. also add a migration anchor: /docs/migrate/routing-policy. can eng add a small paragraph for behavior when using prefix caching?

marc: prefix/KV cache: unchanged. if you rely on aggressive prefix caching and enable prefer_latency, you might see cache misses when routing selects a different model family; we'll call that out. suggested 1-liner: "Note: enabling low-latency routing can increase model-family variance which may reduce prefix cache hit rate; expect small token cost changes."

tom: product request: please add a short sentence about rollout gating — "gradual rollout over 72 hours with automatic rollback on errors" — so support can set expectations.

emily: added. I'll open the PR now against docs-site, branch name: docs/routing-policy-apr-rollout.

deploy-bot: release branch created: refs/heads/docs/routing-policy-apr-rollout by emily (CI checks queued).

emily: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/492 — draft changelog, JS+Python snippets, migration anchor, and known-issue note. tagging @marc for technical signoff and @jason for copy polish.

marc: reviewing now. will add a tiny clarification on partial-stream timing.

jason: copy nit: change "low-latency routing mode" -> "latency-first routing" to match product page. I'll push a small edit.

emily: noted, thanks. plan: merge after tech signoff + a quick smoke doc preview on staging. target merge 2026-04-01.

claire: thank you all. once merged, ops will get the rollout window and support folks get the known-issue note. :raised_hands:

jason: will follow up with a one-paragraph email for the support rotation.

emily: closing loop — I'll add a changelog line to /docs/changelog/2026-04.md as well once PR merges.

claire: great, we're set.
